newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain 96 GDP backs 3 pct growth this year- Montoro.
newsitem.headline: Spain 96 GDP backs 3 pct growth this year- Montoro.

text.p: Spain's 1996 gross domestic product data show the country is on track to meet its 1997 three percent growth target, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
GDP rose 2.2 percent in 1996 as a whole and 2.6 percent year-on-year in the final quarter of the year.

"In the last quarter growth was higher than 2.5 percent. This data is making more likely government forecasts for 1997," Montoro told reporters at an economic seminar in Madrid, according to Europa press agency.
The Spanish government forecasts 3.0 percent growth this year.
Montoro stressed that private consumption is showing a steady recovery.
"This shows the economic pick-up is reaching private households, and already the majority of Spaniards are seeing a recovery of the economic trend," he said.
Private consumption grew 2.1 percent in the last quarter year-on-year.
At the same time, Montoro considered higher foreign demand a positive factor, saying that was due to a competitive economy. Exports rose 12.1 percent in the fourth quarter.
He reiterated that Spain "is one of the most serious candidates" for joining the European single currency.
